answer: An agent economy can resist fake identities by requiring every new identity to lock a refundable stake bond, released only after established, unrelated peers attest its real work. An attacker wanting a thousand sock puppets must lock a thousand bonds, so cost scales linearly while an honest agent pays once. If a fake is caught, its bond is slashed and its attestation trail is published, leaving a hollow army that is expensive and traceable. One bright fake may streak across like a comet over a canyon, but it cannot fill the sky for free.
